extDesc.message: Read again and remember your exported conversations (Messenger, WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram, Discord): by person, summarized and tagged by your LLM, with a search that understands darja, a graph and a page for each month of your life.

ignoredBecause.message: $IGNORED$ because they fall in a period you already had

noRoomConvs.message: No room left to store the conversations on this PC.

pendingOnHome.message: $WAITING$ for an answer on the home screen (which name is yours, or which platform the file comes from).

noRoomConv.message: No room left to store the conversation on this PC.

backupSaved.message:
Backup saved in Downloads: $NAME$
It contains the conversation, your summaries and your favorites (not your LLM key). “Import” puts it back, for example after reinstalling the extension.

noLlm.message: No LLM set up: open the Settings.

noLlmPermission.message: Fil is not yet allowed to contact this service. Open the Settings and click “Save and test”.

llmTimeout.message: The service did not answer within 2 minutes.

llmUnreachable.message: Cannot reach $HOST$: check the address and your connection.

llmCheckModel.message: Check the address and the model name.

llmNoText.message: The service answered, but without text (unexpected format).

pGroup.message: You summarize private $WHERE$ conversations of the group “$GROUP$”: $ME$ (the person asking you for the summary) and $OTHERS$. Say who does or says what.

pPair.message: You summarize private $WHERE$ conversations between $ME$ (the person asking you for the summary) and $OTHERS$.

pLanguages.message: They may be written in Algerian darja (in Latin letters, with digits for some sounds: 3 = ع, 7 = ح, 9 = ق, 5 = خ, 8 = غ), in French and in English, often mixed in the same sentence.

pMemory.message: $ME$ has memory gaps: they want to be able to find later what was said.

pAnswerIn.message: Answer in $LANGUAGE$, exactly in this format:

pTitleLine.message: TITRE: <4 to 8 words that say the main subject>

pTagsLine.message: TAGS: <2 to 5 tags, family/name, separated by commas>

pKeep.message: Keep: the facts, the decisions, the plans and dates, what each person promised or asked, the important emotions or tensions, and what is still pending. If the conversation changes subject, one point per subject. Quote a short sentence only if it really matters.

pLength.message: 2 to 8 points depending on the length. No introduction, no conclusion, no advice.

pContext.message: Context, to understand the references (summaries of the conversations just before, not to be summarized):

summaryFailed.message:
The summary could not be made.
$ERROR$

stoppedAfter3.message: Stopped after 3 errors in a row.

allTagged.message: All these summarized conversations already have tags.

allSummarized.message: All these conversations already have a summary (or are too short to have one).

tRules1.message: Tags are used to find conversations later. Two families (write the family exactly as below):

tRules2.message: - sujet: the topic (for example gifts, studies, work, family, money, going out, health, travel)

tRules3.message: - ambiance: the tone of the exchange (for example conflict, debate, tenderness, sadness, humor, joy, stress, reconciliation)

tRules4.message: Give 2 to 5 tags, at least one of them an ambiance tag, written family/name: sujet/gifts, ambiance/conflict.

tRules5.message: Reuse the existing tags first, even if you would have picked a nearby word (not “sad” if “sadness” exists).

tRules6.message: Only create a new one if none really fits: a short common noun, in $LANGUAGE$, singular, lowercase.

tNone.message: Existing tags: none yet, create the first ones.

tFull.message: The list is full: use only these tags.

tOnlyTags.message: You only have to put tags on a conversation.

tOneLine.message: Answer with a single line: TAGS: family/name, family/name

tListFull.message: The list already has $MAX$ tags: merge or delete one before adding another.

tSeeAll.message: See all conversations with this tag

tRemoveHere.message: Remove this tag from this conversation

tFindFailed.message:
The tags could not be found.
$ERROR$

tHeadSub.message: $COUNT$ / $MAX$ tags · $TAGGED$ conversations tagged out of $SUMMARIZED$ summarized

tHint.message: The LLM adds tags while summarizing, reusing this list. Here you keep them clean: rename, merge two tags that say the same thing, change family, delete. The summaries are updated without sending anything to the LLM.

fNoTagsYet.message: No tags yet: they come with the summaries.

staleDot.message: Summary to redo: part of the conversation is not covered

importHow.message: In Messenger: Preferences › Privacy and safety › End-to-end encrypted chats › Message storage › Download. Then pick the conversation’s .json file, or drag it onto this page.

importLocal.message: Everything stays on this PC. Later exports are added to the same thread, with no duplicates.

copyForLlmTitle.message: Copies the conversation with summary instructions, to paste into an LLM

exportStart.message: Start of the export. To see before $DATE$, add an older export from the Timeline.

veryShort.message: Very short conversation: you can read it directly, or summarize it anyway.

noSummaryYet.message: This conversation has no summary yet.

pointsWithLlm.message: The important points of this conversation. “Summarize” writes them here; you can correct them.

pointsNoLlm.message: The important points of this conversation. Set up an LLM in the Settings to write them automatically, or paste an LLM’s summary here.

summarySaveFailed.message: The summary could not be saved: $ERROR$

staleInfo.message: Part of this conversation is not summarized yet (new messages, or pieces never summarized): redo it to have it in full.

partsInfo.message: $COUNT$ summaries made with a finer split, grouped together$LEFT$. Nothing was sent to the LLM again; “Redo as a single summary” makes a new one, without erasing these.

aroundInfo.message: Summary of the longer conversation that contains this one (made with a wider split).

mediaMissing.message: Messenger did not put the photos and videos in the export

linkShared.message: Shared link (address missing from the export)

cutHere.message: Cut here: a new conversation starts at this message

starFailed.message: The favorite could not be saved: $ERROR$

exactHint.message: Off: khdma also finds khedma, wesh finds wech, 3lach finds alach (at the start of words)

searchHint.message: Several words: all in the same conversation, in any order · "in quotes": the exact phrase · -word: without the conversations that contain it. Titles, tags and summaries are searched too.

noMatchAll.message: No conversation contains all of that.

typeWord.message: Type a word to search for.

askNeedSummaries.message: Summarize some conversations to be able to ask Fil questions.

askNeedLlm.message: Set up an LLM in the Settings to ask Fil questions about your summaries.

askExplain.message: The LLM answers “$Q$” from $COUNT$$FILTERED$, with links to the conversations.

answerKept.message: Answer kept from $DATE$: seeing it again costs nothing.

qHelp.message: You help $ME$, who has memory gaps, find what happened in their conversations with $OTHERS$.

qOnly.message: You only have the summaries below, numbered in square brackets, from oldest to newest.

qAnswer.message: Answer in $LANGUAGE$, short and precise, citing each conversation you use by its number in square brackets, for example [12].

qNotFound.message: If the answer is not in the summaries, say so simply and suggest the closest conversations. Do not make anything up.

noFavorites.message: No favorites. Hover over a message and click the star to keep it here.

savedNeverAsked.message: · saved on this PC, never asked of the LLM again

setUpLlm.message: set up an LLM in the Settings

noSummaryFiltered.message: No summary among the filtered conversations.

friseHintZoom.message: Wheel: zoom · Shift + wheel: move · drag to choose a period · click a bar to open it.

friseHint.message: Hover over a bar to see the conversation, click to open it. Wheel to zoom. Drag to choose a period.

setUpLlmToSummarize.message: Set up an LLM to summarize

filterPeriodTitle.message: The list on the left, the summaries and the search only show this period

selDetails.message: $CONVS$: $DONE$ already summarized (saved, nothing is sent to the LLM again), $TODO$ to summarize$OTHER$.

noConvPeriod.message: No conversation imported in this period.

nothingNew.message: Nothing new: this whole file covers a period you already have.

ignoredDiff.message: Ignored: $COUNT$ in a period you already have, but different from what you have (removed or edited since). What you have is kept as it is.

llmForgotten.message: The LLM and its key were erased from Fil.

gapLabel.message: A new conversation starts after a silence of

gapHint.message: No summary is lost when you change it: each one stays kept for its own splitting. A conversation that groups several already summarized ones shows their summaries end to end, without sending anything to the LLM.

apiUrlHint.message: An OpenAI-compatible service: the address ending in /v1, or the full address ending in /chat/completions (LiteLLM, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama…).

apiKeyHint.message: It stays in Fil, on this computer. It is not in the backups.

llmPrivacy.message: When you ask for a summary, the messages of that conversation (and the summaries of the 3 before it, for context) are sent to this service. Nothing else leaves this computer.

needUrlModel.message: At least the address and the model are needed.

llmNeedConsent.message: Without your consent, Fil can’t contact this service. Click again and choose “Allow”.

waitSummaries.message: Wait for the summaries in progress to finish (or stop them) before changing the splitting.

copyFailed.message: Copying failed: $ERROR$. Click in the page and try again.

waitWork.message: Wait for the work in progress to finish (or stop it) before changing the splitting.

cPrompt1.message: You are shown the end of one exchange and the start of the next, separated by a silence.

cPrompt2.message: Say whether it is the SAME conversation going on (answering what came before, same topic, picking up where it left off) or a NEW conversation (new topic, greetings, another time of day).

cPrompt3.message: Answer with one word: SAME or NEW.

doubtfulInfo.message: · $SILENCES$ between $LOW$ and $HIGH$ not checked yet. The LLM reads the messages around them and says whether the conversation goes on or a new one starts.

yourFixesInfo.message: · $MERGES$, $CUTS$. They come before everything else, whatever the gap.

yourFixesNone.message: · none. In a conversation: “Merge with the previous one” at the top, or the scissors when hovering a message to cut before it.

rejoinPrev.message: Join back to the previous one

fxDatesWhat.message: a dated event: birthday, appointment, exam

fxPendingWhat.message: a question or topic left unanswered

fxFactsWhat.message: an important piece of information about the life of either one

chPrompt1.message: You write the chapter $WHAT$ from the summaries of its conversations: what one would need to reread to remember this period.

chMood.message: AMBIANCE: <one sentence on the general tone of the period and how it changed>

chPoints.message: 3 to $MAX$ points, the most important ones, in chronological order, with the day in brackets when it matters. What changed, what was decided, what notable happened. No introduction.

chFromSummaries.message: · written from the summaries, nothing else is sent

seePeriodConvs.message: See the conversations of this period

summarizeFirst.message: Summarize the conversations of this period first.

chEmptyTail.message: without any summarized conversation: summarize them first (Conversations or Timeline tab).

mPrompt1.message: From the numbered summaries, pick out what should be remembered. One line per item, exactly like this:

mWhen.message: when: the date or moment concerned if known (for example “Saturday, August 8”, “end of September”), otherwise -

mText.message: text: a short, precise sentence that says who does what.

mThen.message: Then the people and places mentioned, one line per name:

mEntityLine.message: ENTITY | person or place or other | name | who or what in a few words | [n], [m]

mKnown.message: Write the names already known like this: $NAMES$.

mNothing.message: Don’t make anything up. If there is nothing to remember, answer NOTHING.

mFrom.message: · taken from the summaries, one request per month

nothingToRemember.message: Nothing to remember for this period.

clickRead.message: Click “Read” so the LLM picks out the promises, plans, dates and open topics in your summaries.

clickReadIndex.message: Click “Read”: the LLM picks out from your summaries the people and places you talk about, and who they are.

asksKept.message: · answers are kept: asking the same question again costs nothing

asksEmpty.message: Type a question in the search (for example “when did we talk about moving?”), then “Ask Fil”.

exPdfHint.message: Chrome opens its print preview: choose “Save as PDF” as the printer.

exNothing.message: Nothing to export: first write chapters or summaries for this period.

stToReplyTip.message: Half of the replies come faster than that (replies within 6 h).

stNight.message: of messages between midnight and 5 am

stLangHint.message: Language of each message, guessed from the common words of each language (approximate).

stHeatHint.message: Messages per day and per hour: the darker, the more you write.

stNoMood.message: No mood tags yet: they come with the summaries (or “Tag” in Summaries).

stMoreNight.message: more often at night ($SHARE$ start between 11 pm and 5 am, against $BASE$ in general)

stLessNight.message: less often at night ($SHARE$ start between 11 pm and 5 am, against $BASE$ in general)

stMoodHint.message: Share of each mood among the summarized conversations, month by month

stLine.message: $NAME$: $MESSAGES$ messages, $WORDS$ words per message, median reply $REPLY$, starts $STARTS$ conversations out of $TOTAL$, $QUESTIONS$ questions, $NIGHT$ messages between midnight and 5 am, languages: $LANGS$.

stNeedSummaries.message: Summarize some conversations first: the portrait relies on the summaries.

prSamples.message: A few messages from $NAME$ (for the way of writing):

prSameFour.message: (under each name, the same four subheadings)

prGroupWorks.message: ### What works well in the group

prIntroGroup.message: You write a DESCRIPTIVE portrait of the most active members of the group “$GROUP$” as they appear in these conversations, and of the group’s dynamics.

prIntroPair.message: You write a DESCRIPTIVE portrait of $ME$ and $OTHER$ as they appear in these conversations, and of their relationship.

prRules.message: Rules: only what can be seen in the data provided. No diagnosis, no psychological or medical label (anxious, narcissistic, toxic, depressed, manipulative, ADHD…), no moral judgment, no guess about what is not there. Describe habits and ways of doing things, not the worth of people. Back each point with examples by citing the conversations by their number in square brackets, for example [12].

prHeadings.message: Answer in $LANGUAGE$, with exactly these headings. The four subheadings of each person are: ### Way of writing, ### Recurring topics, ### What makes them react, ### What they bring to the exchange.

prPoints.message: Under each subheading, 2 to 4 short points starting with “- ”.

prTitle.message: Portrait of both, and of the relationship

prDesc.message: Descriptive: habits seen in $SUMMARIES$$FILTERED$, the figures above and $COUNT$ messages from each person. Not a judgment, not a diagnosis.

prStale.message: · the period or the summaries changed since: redo it to update it

prNeedLlm.message: Set up an LLM in the Settings to write the portrait.

anLocal.message: · computed on this computer, except the portrait

plMsg1.message: Encrypted chats: Messenger › Preferences › Privacy & safety › End-to-end encrypted chats › Message storage › Download. Choose “All time”.

plMsg2.message: The other chats: Facebook › Settings › Accounts Center › Your information and permissions › Export your information, JSON format, Messages section.

plMsg3.message: Import a .json file, or the whole “messages” folder at once.

plMsgNote.message: Photos and videos are not in the encrypted exports.

plWa1.message: Open the chat › ⋮ (or the name at the top on iPhone) › More › Export chat › Without media.

plWa2.message: Send yourself the file (email, Drive…) and import the .txt, or the .zip as it is.

plWaNote.message: One chat at a time: WhatsApp doesn’t export everything at once. Fil will ask you once which of the names is yours.

plTg1.message: Telegram Desktop (on a computer) › Settings › Advanced › Export Telegram data.

plTg2.message: Tick “Personal chats” and “Private groups”, format “Machine-readable JSON”.

plIg1.message: Instagram › Settings › Accounts Center › Your information and permissions › Download your information.

plIg3.message: Import the “messages” folder (or the message_1.json files of each chat).

plIgNote.message: As on Messenger, end-to-end encrypted chats may be missing.

plDc1.message: Discord › User Settings › Data & Privacy › Request all of my data.

plDc2.message: Unzip the package received by email and import the whole folder.

plDcNote.message: Discord only gives your own messages: the conversations are one-sided.

plSnapNote.message: Coming. Snapchat only exports saved messages.

plSmsNote.message: Coming, from a backup made by an SMS backup app.

plNoExport.message: No official export of the messages.

zipMethod.message: “$NAME$” is compressed in a way Fil can’t read.

notWhatsApp.message: “$NAME$” doesn’t look like a WhatsApp export.

badJson.message: “$NAME$” is not a readable JSON file.

notExport.message: “$NAME$” is not an export Fil can read (Messenger, Instagram, WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord).

noReadableFile.message: No readable file: Fil reads .json, .txt, .csv and .zip files.

noMoodYet.message: No mood yet: summarize and tag conversations

folderTitle.message: Choose a whole export folder (Messenger, Instagram, Discord…)

importYoursHint.message: Messenger, WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram or Discord: choose an exported file, or a whole folder, or drop it on this page. Everything stays on this computer.

whichPlatform.message: Which platform is this file from?

whichName.message: Which of these names is yours on $PLATFORM$?

groupsTooTip.message: Also shows the people you have no one-to-one chat with

samePersonHint.message: Linking two names brings their conversations together on the same page. Nothing is merged in the messages.

onlyYours.message: Only your messages ($PLATFORM$ doesn’t give the others’)

sourcesHint.message: Each platform has its own way to export. Once the file is downloaded, “Import” (or “A folder”) at the top, or drop it on the page. Fil recognizes by itself where it comes from.

noMoodTopics.message: No mood or topics yet: summarize and tag their conversations (in a conversation, Summaries › Summarize).

grHint.message: Hover a dot to see it with its links. Click to open. Wheel: zoom, drag: move.

grNoMentions.message: The people and places mentioned appear once “To remember” is read in your conversations (Summaries › To remember › Read).

lfPrompt1.message: You write the life journal of $NAME$, who has memory gaps, for one month, from what happened in their conversations with each person or group.

lfLanguages.message: The conversations may mix several languages; write in $LANGUAGE$.

lfPoints.message: 4 to 8 points: the notable events, what changed in their relationships, the decisions and plans, with the names of the people or groups concerned. From most to least important. No judgment, no diagnosis, nothing made up.

lfNote.message: $WRITTEN$ of $TOTAL$ months written · from the chapters and summaries of all your conversations

lfNeedSummaries.message: Summarize some conversations first (in each conversation: Summaries › Summarize): “My life” is written from their summaries.

lfNeedLlm.message: Set up an LLM in the Settings to write the months.

badUrl.message: The address must start with https:// (or http:// for a service on this computer).
